ground_truth.description: Factory.deploy uses create2 but reverts with CreateCollision if address exists, violating ERC-4337 expectation to return address. Breaks simulations and bundler logic.
ground_truth.root_cause: Factory.deploy uses create2 but reverts with CreateCollision if address exists, violating ERC-4337 expectation to return address. Breaks simulations and bundler logic.
ground_truth.attack_scenario: Deploy wallet once, call deploy again → reverts. Attacker can front-run to cause DoS. PoC: test_factory_double_deploy_PoC in AuditPoC.sol. Shows first deploy succeeds, second reverts.
ground_truth.fix_description: Check if address exists via predicted.code.length, return it if so.

vulnerabilities.explanation: deploy() uses create2 and unconditionally reverts with DeployFailed when the target address already exists (create2 returns 0 on collision). This violates ERC-4337's requirement that factories return the existing address on duplicate deploy calls, breaking simulation, bundler logic, and idempotent deployment expectations.
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario: 1. Legitimate user or bundler calls deploy(_mainModule, _salt) for a new wallet. 2. Attacker front-runs with identical parameters, causing the first tx to succeed and the second to revert. 3. Subsequent calls (including simulations) always revert, preventing wallet creation or account abstraction flows.
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Before create2, compute the predicted address and check if it has code (extcodesize > 0); if so, return the address instead of reverting.

prediction.overall_explanation: The deploy function fails to handle address collisions gracefully, directly contradicting ERC-4337 factory semantics and enabling DoS via front-running or repeated calls.
